F. Property of Mr. Shen Yung Shing.
8 boxes marked S.Y.S. No. 1 to 8, containing:-
Chinese army swords, made in Shanghai.

These swords have been made in Shanghai and form
part of a contract that Mr. Shen Yung Shing made with the
Kiangsi Government - Nanchang - in 1912.-

The swords could not be delivered on account of the
2nd revolution in 1913: no money could be sent down to Shanghai
and the swords thus remained undelivered. Mr. Shen Yung Shing
died shortly afterwards and his partners asked us - respectively
our Compradors - to store the swords in our place to be sold
when occasion offers to do so.-

We have done business with Mr. Shen Yung Shing for
Szechuen in former years in the same line.-

NETHERLANDS CONSULATE-GENERAL,
Shanghai, 2nd April 1917.

No.651.

Sir,

In conformance with the desire verbally expressed by you
to me, although there is no obligation from my side to that
effect, I have complied with that desire in order to give the
least trouble to you and to the German subjects, with the
protection whose interests I have been charged, I have the honour
now to forward to you herewith a list of the German subjects,
which have been registered at this Consulate General at my
intimation. In the list and at the end of it, you will find the
arms, which are in their possession. I enclose also a list of
the removals, which have taken place, and came to my notice since
the closing of the other list and a supplementary list of some arms

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

Consul-General of the Netherlands,
in charge with the protection of
the German interests.

〔此处转录不清〕

Wu Chao-hsin, Esq.,
Special Envoy for Foreign Affairs,
SHANGHAI.
